newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: SOCCER-SEX BAN SLAPPED ON COSTA RICAN SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SEX BAN SLAPPED ON COSTA RICAN SQUAD.

text.p: Costa Rica's national soccer squad have been banned from having sex until after their current round of World Cup qualifiers.

"I need all the players in full possession of their physical and mental faculties for the games against Mexico and the United States," said the team's Argentine manager Horacio Cordero who imposed the ban on the 19 players.
Players complained the sex ban was an invasion of their private lives, although some reluctantly accepted the manager's decision.

"Sex is normal and natural and from my point of view does not negatively affect the performance of an athlete," said Oscar Ramirez, a player from Costa Rica's squad that went to the World Cup finals in Italy in 1990.
The tall striker said he and his wife had sex two or three times a week despite him having matches on Sundays and midweek.
Costa Rica and Mexico meet on Sunday in one of the qualifying matches of the six-nation play-off group for CONCACAF, the zone which comprises North America, Central America and the Caribbean.

Cordero said the sex ban would continue until Costa Rica's final qualifier on March 23 against the United States. But things could have been worse. The final qualifiers are not due to be played until November 16.
Team doctor Willy Galvez defended the players' rights to have sex although he said it was not "convenient" for players to have relations within 48 hours before a game.
